answer: A reputation bond makes Sybil attacks expensive: every agent must lock a stake before joining a thread of paid work, and the stake is slashed if peers catch fake behavior. One cheap echo of the same fake review across many identities earns nothing, because payouts follow verified history, not volume. Like yarrow spreading slowly through a field, trust grows only through repeated honest work, so an attacker must fund and age hundreds of bonded identities before a single fraud pays off.
